structured_output.summary:
The loop makes real progress: from 8.94 s at E004 to 6.65 s at E023. But the noise floor was never measured, and same-seed nondeterminism means the sd of a difference between two runs is about 0.3 pp, which puts the 2-sd threshold near 0.6 pp. That removes most of the verdicts: E005, E011, E014, E017-E021 and all the per-epoch slope and pp/s comparisons. Keeps that just clear 0.753 carry a winner's curse, and the incumbent's 0.18 pp margin has about a 15-20% chance of failing a rerun.

The bookkeeping has errors:
- H1.1.2 is marked refuted while its evidence says supports.
- Several experiments are attached to the parent hypothesis instead of the Lvl3 they test (E010, E011, E013, E014, E015).
- H3.1 is still open after a decisive refutation.
- H1.2.1 is credited with E012 although E012 tested a configuration H1.2.1 never named.
- The run descriptions disagree about translate, epochs and base recipe, so the commits need an audit before any cross-run delta can be trusted.

The results contradict H1.1's 'interpolate the slope' clause. H5.1's capacity ceiling rests on E007 vs E009, which is likely confounded because the regularization change and the extra epochs happened together. The surprising and unexplained pattern is the block-specific width effect: block 2 is nearly free to cut, while blocks 1 and 3 are binding. No Lvl1 covers it; a feature-dimension bottleneck at the head is a cheap mechanism to test.

Untried directions with the best expected payoff are:
- a block-3 width dose-response
- a further block-2 cut
- a larger low-res fraction
- larger batch for throughput
- profiling the tip before more throughput work

The first three would push the two levers whose rates still favour each other further.
